title: Evercove Edge VPC terraform migration assumptions and rollforward (WIP)
content:
Objective:
This is an internal draft playbook for Evercove’s private inference deployment (edge VPC + on-prem peering). Purpose: surface sizing assumptions, Terraform module notes, cutover/rollforward strategy, Q&A with Evercove infra, and acceptance criteria for handoff to Professional Services.

High-level constraints from Evercove call (recorded Nov 2025):
- Latency SLO: P95 inference < 120ms for 1k concurrent chat sessions (avg 64-token responses).
- Regulatory: Data-in-transit must stay inside customer VPC; control plane allowed to talk to Redwood Control Plane over mTLS tunnel.
- Hardware preference: on-prem cluster uses NVIDIA H100 or equivalent; cloud edge uses G5x for pilot.
- KMS: customer uses AWS KMS via a cross-account grant; HSM for signing in phase 2.
- Maintenance windows: nightly 0200–0400 UTC; two-week notice for major upgrades.

Assumptions and sizing rationale (draft):
1) Workload profile
   - 1,000 concurrent chat sessions at peak. Median request size: 512 tokens; median response length: 64 tokens.
   - Token throughput target: ~1k * 64 tokens/s during sustained peaks ≈ 64k tokens/sec.
2) Model selection and performance baseline
   - Initial model: open-bloom-16B-quant (customer wants open weights) configured with 8-bit quantization. Verified locally: 14 tokens/sec per H100 A100-like full-gpu for 16k context (baseline).
   - Use dual model strategy: primary high-quality 16B quantized, fallback 7B distilled for short-tail low-latency paths.
3) GPU count & instance types (edge on-prem design)
   - Baseline: 4 x H100 (large VRAM) per inference cluster for production worker pool. Expected steady-state throughput ~56k tokens/sec aggregated (with batching and KV cache).
   - Buffer for headroom: +25% capacity → provision 5 nodes in prod pool.
   - Staging: 1 H100 node + 1 smaller gpus for canary testing.
4) CPU / Memory / Disk
   - Each worker node: 128 vCPU equivalent, 1.5 TB RAM (for large KV caches and multi-model residency), NVMe 8 TB for local checkpoints and swap.
   - Load balancers and serving agents: t3-equivalent control plane pods (x3).
5) Network
   - VPC CIDR: 10.120.0.0/16 (customer chosen). Edge subnets: 10.120.10.0/24 (workers), 10.120.20.0/24 (control-plane), 10.120.30.0/24 (mgmt/bastion).
   - Transit: AWS TGW peering to on-prem BGP over Direct Connect (BGP AWS ASN 64512 / customer ASN 65000).
   - NLB in front of worker autoscaling group; healthchecks at /healthz (200).

Terraform module notes (names are draft, lives in terraform-modules repo):
- redwood_vpc: creates VPC, subnets, NACLs, route tables. Requires inputs: cidr, az_list, shared_services_account_id.
- redwood_inference_cluster: manages autoscaling groups, launch templates, GPU AMI, instance profiles. Exposes output: worker_asg_name, launch_template_id.
- redwood_kms_grants: helper to create IAM principal grants to use customer KMS. For Evercove, we’ll create a cross-account grant with conditions limited by tag: "redwood:deployment=evercove-edge".
- redwood_remote_state: S3 backend module. MUST enable server-side encryption (SSE-KMS) and DynamoDB locking.
- redwood_tls: provisioning of certs via ACME is disabled for on-prem; expects pre-provisioned certs stored in secret manager.

State management / recommended patterns:
- Remote state: S3 bucket in mfg-account (customer-managed) with SSE-KMS. Use DynamoDB table for locking. Terraform runs must be executed from CI runners inside the customer network or from Redwood-runner with one-time CI tokens.
- Backend naming convention: evercove-prod.tfstate, evercove-staging.tfstate.
- GitOps: Terraform PRs must be gated by automated plan outputs and a single approver from Evercove infra team.

Upgrade and rollforward plan (safe path, minimal downtime):
Phase A — Preflight (week -2 to -1)
  - Review terraform plan in staging. Run full e2e smoke tests (latency, throughput).
  - Confirm KMS cross-account grant and test encryption/decryption with a sample artifact.
  - Snapshot current on-prem VM images and create AMI-equivalent golden images for GPU nodes.
Phase B — Staged rollout (week 0)
  - Create new worker ASG with new launch template (updated runtime). Register with ALB/NLB but mark initial weight 0.
  - Canary traffic (1–2%) routed to canary pool for 24–48 hours. Monitor: p95 latency, error rate, GPU memory trends, kv-cache hit rate.
  - If canary passes, progressively increase to 25%, 50%, 100% (over 2–3 maintenance windows).
Phase C — Fallback & rollforward rules
  - Automatic fallback: requests routed to hosted Redwood-verified fallback model if local pool health degrades > 5% error rate or p95 breach for 15m.
  - Manual rollback: Terraform simply switches instance count or toggles ALB weights to evict new workers and reattach old autoscaling group. State snapshots and AMI rollbacks available.

Operational runbook (short):
- Green light checklist before prod deploy:
  1) DynamoDB state lock table present and verified.
  2) KMS grant tested with sample ciphertext.
  3) TGW BGP sessions established and pref route tables validated.
  4) Canary alerts wired into PagerDuty (P1 if p95 > 180ms for 15 min).
- Incident triage flow:
  1) Identify: check /metrics for 5XX rate and GPU saturations.
  2) Isolate: mark new nodes as draining, reduce ASG desired to 0 for canary group.
  3) Mitigate: enable Redwood-hosted fallback, open support bridge with PS.
  4) Postmortem: collect kernel logs, dmesg, nvml traces; create postmortem in Confluence.

Architecture Q&A log (notes from calls)
Q: Do Evercove ops want the Redwood control-plane in their VPC or hosted?
A: Initially hosted control plane with mTLS tunnel; customer requested ability to move to customer-managed control plane in 6–12 months. Plan: keep control plane traffic minimal (telemetry filtered) and design config to allow control-plane swap via terraform var.

Q: HSM integration timeline?
A: Phase 2. KMS cross-account grant for day 1. HSM for signing keys targeted after compliance signoff (Q2 2026). Implementation notes: use PKCS#11 plugin on control-plane nodes and update redwood_kms_grants module to support keywrap via HSM.

Q: Can we run models in mixed precision across nodes?
A: Yes — runtime supports model shards across quant/float variants. Terraform should tag node pools with "gpu_profile" to ensure scheduler places compatible tasks. Documented in serving-runtime playbook.

Acceptance criteria (must be green BEFORE handoff):
- Throughput: P95 tokens/sec per cluster >= 50k tokens/sec with expected batching profile in staging.
- Latency: P95 inference < 120ms for 64-token responses across 95% of requests in staging.
- Resilience: automatic fallback triggers within 30s and serves traffic with <2x latency increase.
- Security: KMS decrypts for stored caches; all S3 state objects are SSE-KMS encrypted and accessible by approved principals only.

Known gaps & open risks (action items):
- Terraform: module redwood_inference_cluster currently assumes AWS only. Need to add on-prem provider stubs for vSphere/Metal. Owner: Amit P. (Linear RW-1301).
- Autoscaling warmup: system currently scales on CPU/GPU but we need request-based scaling. Add custom metric export for 'queued requests' (RW-1312).
- Cross-account networking edge cases with TGW route propagation when using multiple AZs. Need route table test matrix. Owner: Lucia G.

Quick TODOs (next 2 weeks):
- [ ] Finalize worker instance flavor and confirm procurement lead time with Evercove.
- [ ] Add tf module hooks for HSM (PKCS#11) conditional blocks.
- [ ] Create a runbook excerpt for PS to use during cutover (one-pager).
- [ ] Schedule dry-run migration into customer staging (target: 2025-11-28).

Appendix — Terraform example snippet (conceptual, not copy-paste):
# module "vpc" {
#   source = "github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules//redwood_vpc"
#   cidr = "10.120.0.0/16"
#   azs  = ["us-west-2a","us-west-2b"]
# }
#
# module "inference" {
#   source = "github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules//redwood_inference_cluster"
#   cluster_name = "evercove-prod"
#   gpu_profile  = "h100-xlarge"
#   desired_workers = 5
# }

Notes on documentation handoff:
- Create a short Confluence page that copies the acceptance criteria and the runbook steps. Keep this doc as the engineering draft; flag items resolved and migrate final bits to confluence/PS playbook.

If anything in this doc conflicts with legal or SOC/TPR requirements in the compliance tracker, flag and stop: do not rollout without compliance signoff.

-- maya
